about: Château Gloria is one of the Médoc’s great success stories, built from nothing in a single lifetime. Henri Martin, born in 1903 at Château Gruaud-Larose into a family that had worked Saint-Julien’s vineyards and cellars for three centuries, trained as a cooper. In 1939 he bought his first 6,000 vines beside the family home, and over the following decades he bought only plots from classified growths in Saint-Julien, stitching them into one estate of about 50 hectares. Martin went on to lead Bordeaux’s wine council and to manage Château Latour; his daughter Françoise, her husband Jean-Louis Triaud and their children run Gloria today.

Because it was assembled after 1855, Gloria has never been classified, yet its vineyards lie among the classed growths on deep Günz-era gravel over clay and sand. Cabernet Sauvignon leads, with Merlot, Cabernet Franc and a little Petit Verdot. The wine ages about 14 months in barrel, around 40 percent new. Henri Martin also championed Gloria in the United States, and a 1976 New York Times Magazine article helped make it one of the best-known non-classified wines of Bordeaux.

The 2016, from a celebrated Médoc vintage, is one of Gloria’s finest. Wine Spectator described a core saturated with cassis and blackberry, Jeb Dunnuck called it the best vintage of Gloria he had tasted, and the Wine Advocate praised its depth, ripe tannins and bright acidity. Now about a decade from harvest, it is entering its drinking window while keeping the firm structure that Saint-Julien is known for.
facts: 60% Cabernet Sauvignon, 30% Merlot, 7% Cabernet Franc, 3% Petit Verdot (2016)
Günz gravel over clay and sand
About 14 months in barrel, 40% new oak
About 50 ha assembled from classified-growth plots
